title: Billy Vessels: Oklahoma's First Heisman Trophy Winner in 1952
question: Who was the first Oklahoma Sooner to win the Heisman Trophy?
answer: Halfback Billy Vessels of Cleveland, Oklahoma, won the 1952 Heisman Trophy, the first ever for OU. He ran for 1,072 yards and 17 touchdowns that fall under coach Bud Wilkinson.
summary: Billy Vessels won OU's first Heisman in 1952 with 1,072 rushing yards, then built a second career in Florida real estate and horse racing regulation.
body: Every Sooner Heisman story starts with Billy Vessels. A halfback from Cleveland, Oklahoma, he played for Bud Wilkinson from 1950 through 1952 and was part of the 1950 team that finished as consensus national champions. Two years later he became the first Oklahoma player to take home college football's most famous trophy.

His 1952 senior season was a showcase. Vessels carried 161 times for 1,072 yards and 17 rushing touchdowns, and the Heisman Trust credits him as the first winner of the award to top 1,000 rushing yards. He also led the nation in all-purpose yardage. His signature performance came in a 27-21 loss at Notre Dame, the only defeat of OU's 8-1-1 season, when he gained 195 yards on 17 carries and scored all three Sooner touchdowns.
The voting was not close. Vessels collected 525 points, well ahead of Maryland's Jack Scarbath at 367.

Pro football took him north first. After the Baltimore Colts made him a first-round pick in 1953, he signed with the Edmonton Eskimos and won the Schenley Award as the top player in Canadian football as a rookie. Following Army service, he played one season with the Colts in 1956 before retiring.

His second act was in South Florida, where he worked as a real estate executive and horse breeder. He became a leader in racing regulation, serving with the Florida agency that oversaw parimutuel wagering and, in 1984, being elected president of the national association of racing commissioners. Vessels entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1974 and died in 2001.
